services.title: Issuance of the People of Determination Card
services.description: The People of Determination Card is an identity card issued by the Ministry of Family to persons with disabilities. It serves as an official document confirming that the holder is a person with a disability, ensuring the rights granted under Federal Law No. (29) of 2006 on Persons with Disabilities, as well as the regulations and decisions issued in its implementation.
services.audience: Emirati citizens and residents in the UAE from the People of Determination category
terms: Must be an Emirati citizen or a legally resident in the UAE.
Must have medical or psychological reports confirming the disability from an accredited official authority, such as a government hospital.
documents: Medical report (for physical and sensory disabilities) and psychological report (for intellectual, psychological disabilities, attention deficit hyperactivity disorder, autism, and learning difficulties) from an accredited official authority confirming the presence of the disability.
Passport-size photo with a white background.

services.title: Disability Type Change
services.description: A service that enables People of Determination to request a change to the type of disability registered in their records with the Ministry, based on approved medical documents and reports reflecting the applicant's current condition.
services.audience: Emirati citizens and residents in the UAE from the People of Determination
terms: Availability of a previously issued People of Determination Card from the Ministry
documents: A recent photograph with a white background.

services.title: Registration in People of Determination Care and Rehabilitation Centers and Early Intervention Units Centers
services.description: This service allows the registration of children with developmental delays and those at risk of disability (People of Determination) to enroll in Early Intervention Centers and Units during early childhood. It also enables the registration of People of Determination in rehabilitation centers upon reaching the age of 4 to receive a range of rehabilitation and educational services, in addition to support and guidance programs provided by a specialized team to empower them and their families, enhance their skills, integrate them into society, and improve their quality of life
services.audience: Emirati citizens and children of female nationals
terms: The child must be under five years of age.
documents: Copy of the medical report (if available)
Children of female nationals (Copy of the child's birth certificate and the mother's passport or ID).
Personal Photo

services.title: Application for a license for non-governmental family counseling centers
services.description: A service that individuals and companies apply for to obtain a license to conduct family counseling activities aimed at improving the quality of family life and ensuring its stability. These services include: family and social counseling, educational counseling, workshops, and therapeutic and training plans. (Economic Activity: Social and Family Counseling) Matchmaking services for those wishing to marry, aimed at guiding and advising those about to marry and facilitating matchmaking. (Economic Activity: Services of Marriage Bureaux)
services.fees: License for non-governmental Family Counseling Center Fees: 5,000 AED
terms: The license applicant must be an individual, although a legal entity may also apply if it takes one of the company forms specified in the Commercial Companies Law.

The applicant must hold a university degree accredited in Special Education, Psychology, Counseling and Mental Health, Sociology, Social Work, or other related scientific fields in family affairs from a recognized university in the UAE.
The applicant must be at least thirty (30) years old and fully legally competent.
The applicant must not have previously been convicted of a felony or a dishonesty-related misdemeanor, even if their rights of rehabilitation have been restored.
The applicant must not have a history of license revocation due to non-compliance in the past three years.
The institution must provide suitable premises that meet all technical, engineering, health, and environmental requirements approved by the relevant authorities.
documents: Emirates ID
Academic Qualification
Good Conduct Certificate (Criminal Record) for the applicant and partners – if applicable
Building plan showing the dimensions and measurements of rooms, halls, corridors, and sanitary facilities
Copy of the property deed for the site or a copy of the lease agreement

Additional Documents for Companies: Copy of the commercial license issued by the competent authorities in the UAE, the company's Articles of Association, and valid residency permits for the company owners
Permit from the Civil Defense confirming compliance with fire prevention and safety requirements
Copy of the commercial or professional license from the Department of Economic Development
Information of the center director, their academic qualifications, and copies of experience certificates

extra.title: Requirements for Obtaining a License to Provide Matchmaking Services:
items: The applicant must be a UAE national and the sole owner of the center.
The applicant must hold at least a high school diploma or its equivalent.
The center's activity must be limited to providing matchmaking services only.
The applicant must comply with conditions (3), (4), (5), and (6) stated in the previous section.

services.title: Marriage Grant Application
services.description: A package of social services aimed at building stable and cohesive families equipped with the knowledge and skills needed to establish positive and sustainable marital relationships. In addition, couples receive a financial grant of seventy thousand dirhams to support them in starting a happy and stable life.
terms: Both the applicant and his wife must be UAE nationals.
The groom must not be less than twenty-one (21) years old and the bride must not be less than eighteen (18) years old at the time of the marriage contract.
The applicant's monthly net income must not exceed AED 25,000 (twenty-five thousand dirhams), after deducting pension contributions and housing allowance (if any).
The grant application must be submitted within a period not exceeding six months from the date of the marriage contract.

The grant applicant and his wife must commit to attending the mandatory awareness courses and lectures of the Premarital Preparation Program (Edaad) within one year from the date of submitting the marriage grant application.
The grant applicant must complete and submit the required documents within a period not exceeding three months from the date of application submission.
The applicant must not have previously benefited from the Marriage Grant or from any other grant in the UAE.

The grant applicant must not be married, unless exempted in accordance with the provisions of Clause (3) of Article (4) of Cabinet Resolution No. (5) of 2017 regarding the conditions, regulations, and procedures for disbursing the Marriage Grant.
documents: Document proving the applicant's monthly net income, including a detailed salary certificate (the basic salary certificate should include allowances, bonuses, housing allowance, and pension deductions).
Statement of land and property ownership from the passport issuing authority, in addition to a statement from the Department of Planning and Survey (for applicants from Sharjah only).
Bank statement showing the applicant's monthly salary deposits, indicating the account balance for the last three months prior to the submission date on the website.
Bank confirmation letter including the International Bank Account Number (IBAN).

Within one calendar year from the date of grant disbursement, the beneficiary must submit the original or a certified true copy from the competent court of the legal entry acknowledgment in the presence of the spouse or her guardian, or the child's birth certificate, or a copy of the child's addition.

terms: Priority is given to those who do not meet the conditions and regulations of the Marriage Grant Service
The applicant must not have previously participated in a mass wedding

extra.title: Service definition
items: Early Intervention Services: Supportive educational, therapeutic, and rehabilitation services for children from birth up to 6 years of age with disabilities, developmental delays, or at risk of disability. (Economic Activity: Early educational and rehabilitation services)
Integrated Service: Educational and therapeutic services for persons with disabilities following a school-like system for ages 4 to 18 years. (Economic Activity: Special education services)
Vocational Rehabilitation Service: Specialized services in training, rehabilitation, employment, and follow-up for ages 16 to 35 years. (Economic Activity: Vocational rehabilitation services)

Life Skills Service: Training in specific skills suitable to the type and degree of disability, provided to persons with disabilities over 18 years of age. (Economic Activity: Daily life skills services for People of Determination)

Individual Therapeutic Rehabilitation Sessions: Services provided as individual therapy sessions, including speech-language therapy, occupational therapy, special education, behavior modification programs, psychological assessment, and family counseling. (Economic Activity: Therapeutic service centers and psychological assessment)

Educational and Psychological Assessment Service: A set of procedures and tests to evaluate cognitive and intellectual abilities to determine the appropriate educational needs. (Economic Activity: Therapeutic service centers and psychological assessment)

news.title: Cabinet Resolution Regarding Regulating Children's Access to Social Media Platform
news.brief: / /Cabinet Resolution Regarding Regulating Children's Access to Social Media Platform 19 June 2026This resolution establishes a regulatory framework for children's access to social media platforms in the UAE. It defines which platforms fall within scope, sets the minimum age for personal accounts, introduces age-verification requirements, and outlines the responsibilities of platforms, caregivers, and relevant authorities.

faq.question: Why is the UAE introducing new measures to regulate children's access to social media?
answer: The UAE is introducing an age-appropriate access framework that regulates children's access to social media in a safer, more balanced, and developmentally aligned way. The aim is to create an environment where children can benefit from technology without being exposed too early to its risks. The framework sets a minimum age of 15 for personal accounts, applies enhanced safeguards for those aged 15 to under 16, and allows structured participation in non-harmful content under specific conditions. Ultimately, this is about protecting childhood, supporting families, and ensuring that technology serves children's wellbeing and development in a balanced way.

faq.question: Why is the UAE introducing this resolution now?
answer: Children today are growing up in an increasingly digital environment that offers both opportunity and evolving risks. As platforms and technologies become more embedded in daily life, there is a need for a proactive national framework that can guide policy, monitor risks, and coordinate efforts across relevant entities. At the same time, it is important to respond to growing concerns around children's development and wellbeing, while ensuring that their growth continues to be shaped by balanced exposure not only to technology, but also to real-world social, learning, and cultural experiences.

This resolution reflects the UAE's commitment to acting early to protect children while ensuring they continue to benefit from technology in a safe, balanced, and responsible way, without losing connection to the developmental foundations and embodied cultural experiences that remain essential during childhood.

faq.question: What message does this resolution send about the UAE's broader vision for children, families, and the digital future?
answer: This resolution reflects the UAE's commitment to ensuring that children grow up in a digital environment that is safe, balanced, and aligned with national values. It demonstrates a forward-looking approach that not only addresses current challenges but also shapes a healthier and more age-appropriate digital future. It reinforces the importance of strong families, coordinated national action, and responsible digital engagement in supporting children's development and confidence.

faq.question: How does this support families and parents, and what practical changes should they expect in the coming months?
answer: This resolution supports families by placing practical guidance, awareness, and accessible tools at the center of the national response. Parents can expect clearer direction on safe digital use, stronger support on issues such as parental controls and screen-time balance, and increased awareness of online risks. The approach is designed to support parents rather than burden them, with platforms taking primary responsibility for enforcing safeguards while families are better equipped to guide their children confidently.

faq.question: What support will be available to help children and families transition toward healthier digital habits, especially for those already used to social media?
answer: The resolution recognizes that many children are already accustomed to social media as part of their daily routine, and that change needs to be supported, not imposed abruptly. This is why the approach focuses on gradual transition, practical guidance, and helping families identify positive alternatives, rather than simply restricting access.

Families will be supported through awareness materials, guidance, and tools that encourage healthier digital habits alongside alternative activities, such as sports, creative pursuits, learning opportunities, and safe, age-appropriate digital content. The aim is to help children manage boredom, build new routines, and engage more meaningfully with their surroundings during this transition.

This is part of a broader effort to support children's wellbeing by balancing digital engagement with real-world social, cultural, and developmental experiences, while ensuring that platforms take responsibility for enforcing safeguards and families are supported throughout the process.

faq.question: What role will schools play in helping children build safer digital habits?
answer: Schools are key partners in this effort. The resolution supports the integration of digital safety into educational and awareness activities, alongside training programs that help children understand safe and responsible online behavior. It also ensures that teachers and caregivers are equipped with the tools and guidance needed to reinforce positive digital habits.

faq.question: One of the biggest concerns in UAE households is gaming addiction, late-night scrolling, and excessive screen time. How does this resolution address that?
answer: The resolution directly addresses behaviours such as excessive screen time, late-night use, and compulsive engagement with high-risk features. For users aged 15 to under 16, platforms are required to implement age-appropriate safeguards, including limits on access times, tools to manage usage, restrictions on interactions with unknown users, and tighter controls on high-risk features such as unrestricted messaging, live streaming, and intensive algorithmic recommendations.

faq.question: Can this be viewed as restricting access to technology and digital innovation for children?
answer: This is not about limiting access to technology. This is about making access safer and more age-appropriate. The resolution is designed to ensure that children can benefit from technology in ways that support their development and wellbeing, without being exposed too early to the risks associated with unrestricted social media use.

This is about creating a balanced digital environment where children can benefit from technology while also having the space to build their cultural identity, values, and real-world social connections, without being exposed too early to its risks.

faq.question: Which platforms are included under this resolution?
answer: In the current phase, the resolution applies to the following social media platforms: X, Facebook, Instagram, Snapchat, and TikTok.

faq.question: How will this affect social media platforms and what will they need to do to comply?
answer: Platforms will be required to implement reliable age-verification mechanisms, prevent children under 15 from maintaining personal accounts, and apply enhanced safeguards for those aged 15 to under 16. They will also need to prevent circumvention, provide parental tools, conduct periodic child-safety risk assessments, and comply with reporting requirements. Further guidelines will support platforms in aligning with the resolution.

faq.question: Will platforms be fined if they fail to protect children?
answer: The resolution makes clear that enforcement sits with the competent authorities, and it links violations to the broader child digital safety legal framework rather than creating a separate standalone penalty schedule inside this decision itself. Relevant authorities will take necessary measures upon proven violation or negligence, including administrative penalties and even partial or full blocking in serious cases, under the existing resolution-law and its administrative sanctions framework.

faq.question: What if children simply move to another app, gaming chat, or use a parent's account?
answer: While no system can eliminate all workarounds, the resolution significantly raises the level of protection. Platforms are required to implement effective age-verification measures, detect and disable non-compliant accounts, and take reasonable steps to reduce circumvention. At the same time, caregivers play an important role in ensuring that safeguards are not bypassed, reinforcing a shared responsibility approach. This also needs to be supported by helping families identify healthier alternatives, so that children are better able to deal with the boredom or frustration that can sometimes come with changing digital habits.

faq.question: How does this resolution protect children's privacy and data without leading to intrusive monitoring?
answer: Privacy protection is embedded within the resolution. Age-verification systems are required to collect only the minimum necessary data, ensure secure processing, and avoid retaining sensitive data beyond what is strictly required. The approach is designed to provide effective protection without introducing intrusive monitoring.

faq.question: How will age verification work in practice?
answer: The resolution allows for multiple approved age-verification methods, provided they are effective, reliable, proportionate, and privacy-respecting. These may include government digital identity, ID verification, biometric matching, or AI-based estimation. What is explicitly not acceptable is simple self-declaration without proper assurance.

faq.question: What happens to children who already have accounts today? Will they lose access forever?
answer: For children under 15, personal social media accounts covered by the resolution will no longer be permissible and must be disabled by platforms. For those aged 15 to under 16, access remains allowed but subject to enhanced safeguards, with a 12-month transition period to enable implementation.

faq.question: How is this different from existing cybercrime and child protection laws?
answer: This resolution is different because it is preventive and regulatory, not only punitive. Existing cybercrime and child protection laws are essential, but they mainly address harm after it occurs or prohibit clearly unlawful conduct. This resolution goes further upstream by setting age-based access rules, verification requirements, platform obligations, parental responsibilities, and safety-by-design measures before harm occurs.

faq.question: When will this actually start, and when should parents and platforms expect the first visible changes?
answer: The resolution will come into force following publication in the Official Gazette, with a transition period of up to 12 months for platforms to align their systems and controls. This allows for phased implementation, with visible changes expected to roll out progressively during this period.

faq.question: Why was the cut-off set at 15 years old?
answer: There is no single universally agreed 'perfect age' for social media access, because young people's maturity, vulnerability, and online experiences differ, The resolution takes a practical approach by strengthening protection during earlier teenage years while avoiding unnecessary disruption for older users. It also aligns with existing UAE regulatory thresholds, ensuring consistency across the broader framework.

faq.question: How does this compare to other countries' approaches? Is the UAE going further?
answer: The UAE is aligned with global momentum on child digital safety, where multiple countries are introducing stronger safeguards for minors online. What distinguishes the UAE approach is its balanced and structured model, combining age thresholds, platform accountability, parental enablement, and privacy-conscious verification. Rather than a single restriction, it introduces a comprehensive system-level framework that is both protective and practical to implement.

faq.question: Is the UAE planning to coordinate this internationally?
answer: The UAE sees strong value in international collaboration on this issue. Children's digital environments are inherently cross-border, and effective solutions benefit from coordination between countries. The UAE is open to engaging with like-minded partners to share learnings, align approaches where appropriate, and contribute to shaping global best practices on child digital safety.

faq.question: Will this impact innovation or discourage platforms from operating in the UAE?
answer: The resolution is designed to provide clarity, not constraint. By setting clear and predictable expectations, it enables platforms to operate confidently while aligning with child safety standards. The UAE remains a strong environment for innovation, and this framework ensures that innovation evolves in a way that is responsible and sustainable.

faq.question: What costs or operational burden will this place on platforms?
answer: There will be an initial implementation effort, particularly around age assurance and safety features. However, many leading platforms are already moving in this direction globally. The 12-month transition period allows for phased, practical implementation, and further guidance will support platforms in aligning efficiently.

faq.question: How will the government ensure consistent enforcement across global platforms?
answer: Enforcement will be anchored in the UAE's existing regulatory and legal framework, supported by competent authorities and coordinated oversight. The focus is on clear compliance expectations, monitoring, and proportionate enforcement measures where necessary. The aim is not only enforcement but also sustained compliance through engagement and guidance.

faq.question: What happens if parents disagree with the policy or choose not to comply?
answer: The resolution is designed to support families rather than penalize them. The primary enforcement focus is on platforms. At the same time, parents are encouraged to play a supportive role in guiding children's digital behavior. The approach is based on shared responsibility, awareness, and support, rather than punitive action toward families.

faq.question: How does this consider children's voices and perspectives?
answer: The broader approach includes engagement with stakeholders across the ecosystem, including educators, families, child-focused experts, and those who work closely with children's needs and experiences. The intention is to ensure that policies reflect not only protection needs but also children's developmental, social, and learning needs.

Going forward, children's perspectives will continue to be taken into account, with future policy development informed by engagement approaches that are appropriate to their age, wellbeing, and best interests.

Shifting demographics, economic pressures, and evolving social norms are reshaping family life.

## A Vision Rooted in Strong Values
The UAE’s vision for a resilient, inclusive society depends on strong families. They are where
values are lived, belonging is built, and futures begin.
To realize this vision, the UAE leadership shaped a ministry dedicated to family. The Ministry of
Family was established in December 2024, reflecting a deep understanding of the evolving
dynamics shaping family life in the UAE and across the globe.

On December 8, 2024, His Highness Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, Vice President,
Prime Minister of the UAE, and Ruler of Dubai, announced the establishment of the Ministry
of Family in the UAE. This initiative came under the directives of UAE President His
Highness Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan.
The Ministry is mandated to propose, develop, and implement policies, strategies, and
legislation related to building stable and cohesive families in the UAE. Its objectives
include strengthening the family’s role in effective upbringing, reinforcing national
identity, and promoting positive values and behaviours within the community.

A package of social services aimed at building stable and cohesive families equipped with the knowledge and skills needed to establish positive and sustainable marital relationships. In addition, couples receive a financial grant of seventy thousand dirhams to support them in starting a happy and stable life.
LINK|/en/services/to-whom-it-may-concern-certificate/|Issuance of a To Whom It May Concern Certificate

A service that enables individuals to request a "To Whom It May Concern" certificate from the Ministry, indicating the status of their Marriage Grant application or their beneficiary status, based on the records available with the Ministry.
LINK|/en/services/determination-card/|Issuance of the People of Determination Card

The People of Determination Card is an identity card issued by the Ministry of Family to persons with disabilities. It serves as an official document confirming that the holder is a person with a disability, ensuring the rights granted under Federal Law No. (29) of 2006 on Persons with Disabilities, as well as the regulations and decisions issued in its implementation.
LINK|/en/services/family-counseling-centers-licensing/|Application for a license for non-governmental family counseling centers

A service that individuals and companies apply for to obtain a license to conduct family counseling activities aimed at improving the quality of family life and ensuring its stability. These services include: family and social counseling, educational counseling, workshops, and therapeutic and training plans. (Economic Activity: Social and Family Counseling) Matchmaking services for those wishing to marry, aimed at guiding and advising those about to marry and facilitating matchmaking. (Economic Activity: Services of Marriage Bureaux)
LINK|/en/services/family-counseling-centers-ad-publication/|Request to publish an advertisement for non-governmental family counseling centers

Granting approval to publish promotional advertisements for the services and programs offered by non-governmental Family Counseling Centers, ensuring alignment with their objectives, services, and programs.
LINK|/en/services/pod-card-replacement/|Request for Issuance of a Replacement for a Lost or Damaged People of Determination Card
Issuance of a replacement for a lost or damaged People of Determination Card to ensure continued access to services and facilities across various entities and sectors in the UAE.

A service that enables People of Determination to request a change to the type of disability registered in their records with the Ministry, based on approved medical documents and reports reflecting the applicant's current condition.
LINK|/en/services/non-government-pod-institutions-licensing/|Application for Licensing Non-Governmental People of Determination Institutions

Licensing of Non-Governmental Institutions to Conduct Activities and Provide Services for People of Determination, including early intervention services, integrated service, vocational rehabilitation service, life skills service, individual therapeutic rehabilitation sessions, and educational and psychological assessment service.
LINK|/en/services/non-government-pod-institutions-license-renewal/|Application for Renewal of Non-Governmental People of Determination Rehabilitation Institution License
Updating and renewing the application to legally and regularly continue the activities and services of People of Determination Care and Rehabilitation Centers.
LINK|/en/services/mass-wedding-participation/|Application to Participate in the Mass Wedding

A social model derived from Emirati heritage in organizing mass wedding ceremonies, aligned with the authentic values and principles of society that reflect solidarity and social cohesion, enabling couples to begin a stable married life and build cohesive and sustainable families.
LINK|/en/services/family-counseling-centers-license-renewal/|Application for renewal of license for non-governmental family counseling centers
Updating and renewing the application to legally and regularly continue the activities and services of the Private Family Counseling Center.
LINK|/en/services/pod-care-rehab-centers-registration/|Registration in People of Determination Care and Rehabilitation Centers

A service that enables People of Determination to register at the Ministry's Centers for the Care and Rehabilitation of People of Determination upon reaching the age of five, with the aim of accessing specialized care and rehabilitation services tailored to their individual needs and type of disability, subject to an assessment of their condition and fulfillment of the approved admission requirements and criteria.
LINK|/en/services/early-intervention-centers-registration/|Registration in People of Determination Care and Rehabilitation Centers and Early Intervention Units Centers

This service allows the registration of children with developmental delays and those at risk of disability (People of Determination) to enroll in Early Intervention Centers and Units during early childhood. It also enables the registration of People of Determination in rehabilitation centers upon reaching the age of 4 to receive a range of rehabilitation and educational services, in addition to support and guidance programs provided by a specialized team to empower them and their families, enhance their skills, integrate them into society, and improve their quality of life
